newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank 182-day BBC sold at 2.36 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank 182-day BBC sold at 2.36 pct.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank sold 452 million reais of 182-day Central Bank Bonds (BBC) Tuesday at an overnight rate of 2.36 percent a month, dealers said.
It was the first time the Central Bank sold 182-day BBC bonds since April 22, and was seen as a test by the bank on what rate level the market would demand for longer-dated paper.
Tuesday's auction result was somewhat higher than the market expected, dealers said.

On April 29, the Central Bank offered 1.5 billion reais of 182-day BBCs, but did not grant the rates asked by the market and did not sell them. Last week, the Central Bank did not even offer 182-day BBCs.
On those two occasions, the bank was reluctant to accept higher interest rates which the market was demanding after the bank left rates unchanged in May, reversing an eight-month policy of rate cuts.
The decision to leave rates unchanged was followed by credit restrictions, which caused the market to further speculate about how high long-term rates would go.
At Tuesday's auction, the Central Bank also sold 3.881 billion reais in 56-day BBCs at an overnight rate of 2.326 percent a month, down from 2.348 percent last week.
The financial result of the auction indicated 333 million reais will be drained from the banking system as 4.0 billion reais in 56-day old bonds come due Wednesday.
